findings.evidence: htt/src/common/pr182_parity_registry.py:26 registers 'sign(EB/TB) = sign(x_h)'; :27-32 falsifier compares it to local velocity-curl handedness. But I2 (pr182_sympy_axis.py:49-81, verified on all 4 axes) proves reflection flips BOTH TB and EB, so a helical VII_h model and its mirror predict the identical sign(EB/TB) — the ratio carries zero handedness information. I3 (pr182_sympy_axis.py:84-98) itself shows the improper transform maps n->-n (and a->-a), leaving n2*n3 and a^2 — hence h and any x_h — orientation-EVEN; in the standard VII_h convention h>0 so sign(x_h) is identically +1. Fix: register sign(TB) (or sign(EB)) individually against a signed-handedness template convention. Also propagated to docs/generated/pr182_result_card.json:76 and pr182_spec.yaml:110.
findings.summary: Headline registry relation sign(EB/TB)=sign(x_h) is internally refuted by the PR's own verified identities I2+I3: EB/TB is parity-even (handedness-blind) while velocity-curl handedness is parity-odd, and x_h is orientation-even (h=a^2/(n2 n3)>0 is invariant under n->-n, a->-a). The falsifier semantics can never bind; the PR's sole novel sliver is vacuous as registered. Borderline P0.

findings.evidence: pr182_sympy_axis.py:35-46 obligation key 'axisymmetric_source_forces_B_zero' names a mirror-fixed-sector fact; spec claim (pr182_spec.yaml:33-35) says 'mirror-fixed axisymmetric sector' but registry entry 2 (:120) and the I4 chain (:39-41 'axisymmetric ... hence by I1/I2 no parity-odd boost signal') drop the mirror condition. The pure_boost registry entry (:44-53) derives 'parity-odd TB/EB identically zero' for polarized transport from a temperature-only kernel identity. Conclusion is physically right for a boost; the registered derivation chain is a sketch, and 'theorem' overstates it.
findings.summary: The 'axisymmetric => B=0' reduction smuggles the hard content: what is CAS-verified is the nullspace of diag(1,-1)-I on an abstract 2-vector; the spin-2 reflection law justifying P=diag(1,-1) on the m=0 (E,B) doublet is assumed on every axis, and the obligation name drops the required mirror-symmetry (O(2) vs SO(2)) condition — axisymmetry alone does NOT force B=0 (a tangential 45-degree curl pattern about the axis is an axisymmetric pure-B field). The I4 mu-only check is additionally vacuous by construction, and the 'no parity-odd boost signal' inference covers only the temperature Doppler kernel, not spin-2 aberration of polarization.

notes: The four CAS identities verify as encoded (SymPy axis re-run live: all seven obligations pass; boost coefficients are the correct Taylor data for sqrt(1-b^2)/(1-b*mu); diag(1,1,-1) on (T,E,B) spectra is the standard parity action; the four-axis blinding/adjudication mechanics and the no-data-ingestion guard are sound). The failure is in meaning, not arithmetic: (1) the PR's only novel content — the handedness reference relation sign(EB/TB)=sign(x_h) — is refuted by the PR's own I2 (both TB and EB flip, so the ratio is handedness-blind) and I3 (h is orientation-even), making the registered falsifier structurally unable to bind (P1, borderline P0; trivially fixable by registering sign(TB)/sign(EB) individually against a signed-handedness convention); (2) the Pontzen-Challinor identifier 'PRD 96, 023532' is fabricated (actual: MNRAS 380, 1387, arXiv:0706.2075) and the 'per roadmap' provenance is false; (3) VII_0 is misclassified as an axisymmetric B=0 class.
